pick.headline: Beirut magazine exposes McFarlane's secret trip to Tehran
pick.summary: On 3 November 1986 the Beirut weekly Ash-Shiraa reported that former US National Security Adviser Robert McFarlane had secretly visited Tehran, revealing American arms sales to Iran.
pick.significance: The story broke open the Reagan administration's covert arms-for-hostages dealings with Iran, contradicting its public embargo and its refusal to bargain with hostage-takers. It led within weeks to the discovery that profits had been diverted to the Nicaraguan contras.
pick.fbis: FBIS's regional review reported that Majlis Speaker Hashemi-Rafsanjani, speaking at a Tehran rally on the embassy seizure anniversary, gave details of McFarlane's visit, saying the Americans had arrived in a cargo plane bearing a message from Reagan.

alternates.headline: Mercenaries attempt a coup in the Maldives; India intervenes
alternates.summary: On 3 November 1988 Sri Lankan Tamil mercenaries attacked Male in an attempt to overthrow President Maumoon Abdul Gayoom. Indian paratroops flown in that night put down the attempt.
alternates.significance: India's swift intervention, at Gayoom's request, showed New Delhi acting as the security guarantor of the Indian Ocean region, and Washington and London welcomed it.
alternates.fbis: Delhi radio's English service reported on the morning of 3 November that unidentified gunmen had attacked the presidential palace in Male, and that President Gayoom and his ministers were safe.
